chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi', from Mufaddal ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

It is upon you to acquire deep understanding (tafaqquh) in the religion of God, and do not become like Bedouins. For indeed, whoever does not acquire deep understanding in the religion of God — God will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection, and will not purify any deed of his.

key_terms.أعراب: Bedouins — used here metaphorically for those who are religiously ignorant or untrained in the scholarly tradition
key_terms.التفقه: Tafaqquh — deep, scholarly understanding of Islamic law and theology, beyond surface-level practice
key_terms.لم يزك له عملا: Will not purify his deed — God will not accept or sanctify the religious actions of the ignorant person
key_terms.لم ينظر الله إليه: God will not look at him — a Quranic idiom signifying divine disregard and withdrawal of mercy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the obligation of acquiring deep understanding (tafaqquh) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a stern warning to his companions: they must commit to deeply understanding Islamic religion (tafaqquh), not merely following it superficially like the Bedouin Arabs who lacked scholarly grounding. The gravity of neglecting this is severe — on the Day of Judgment, God will not regard such a person with mercy and will not sanctify their deeds. This teaching reflects the early Shia emphasis on combining authentic narration with deep juridical and theological understanding, as embodied in the Imams' school.
